questions.question: At which OSI layer do routers primarily operate?
questions.explanation: Routers operate at Layer 3 (Network), making forwarding decisions based on IP addresses. Switches operate at Layer 2 using MAC addresses.

questions.question: A load balancer inspects HTTP headers to route requests to different backend services. At which OSI layer is it operating?
questions.explanation: Inspecting HTTP headers requires understanding application-level protocols, which is Layer 7. Layer 4 load balancers only see TCP/UDP ports, not HTTP content.

questions.question: Which OSI layers are typically handled by the operating system's network stack? (Choose all that apply)
questions.explanation: The OS kernel handles Layer 3 (IP) and Layer 4 (TCP/UDP). Layer 1 is hardware (NICs, cables). Layer 7 is handled by applications. Layer 2 is split between hardware and drivers.

questions.question: A firewall blocks traffic based on source/destination IP and port numbers. Which OSI layers is it inspecting?
questions.explanation: IP addresses are Layer 3 (Network), port numbers are Layer 4 (Transport). This describes a stateful packet filter. Deep packet inspection (Layer 7) would examine application data.

questions.question: TLS/SSL encryption operates at which OSI layer?

options.text: Between Layer 4 and Layer 7 (often called Layer 5/6)

questions.explanation: TLS sits between TCP (Layer 4) and application protocols (Layer 7). It's often described as Layer 5/6, handling session establishment and data encryption/presentation.

questions.question: Which statement about Layer 4 vs Layer 7 load balancing is correct?

options.text: Layer 4 is always faster because it inspects less data
Layer 7 can route based on URL paths; Layer 4 cannot
Layer 4 can terminate SSL; Layer 7 cannot
Layer 7 is required for TCP load balancing

questions.explanation: Layer 7 LBs understand HTTP and can route by URL, headers, cookies. Layer 4 only sees IP/port. Both can terminate SSL. Layer 4 handles TCP without understanding the application protocol.

questions.question: A network issue causes packet loss. At which layer would you first investigate?

options.text: Layer 1/2 - Check physical connections and switch ports
Start from Layer 1 and work up

questions.explanation: Network troubleshooting typically starts at lower layers: physical connections (L1), link errors (L2), then routing (L3), then transport (L4). This bottom-up approach isolates the problem layer.

questions.question: Which protocols operate at Layer 4 (Transport)? (Choose all that apply)
questions.explanation: TCP and UDP are Layer 4 transport protocols. HTTP is Layer 7 (Application). IP is Layer 3 (Network).

questions.question: An API gateway performs request routing, authentication, and rate limiting. Which OSI layer best describes its operation?
questions.explanation: API gateways operate at Layer 7, understanding HTTP/HTTPS, parsing requests, checking auth tokens, and making routing decisions based on application-level data.

questions.question: True or False: The OSI model perfectly maps to how modern internet protocols are implemented.
questions.explanation: The OSI model is a conceptual framework. Real protocols often span multiple layers or don't fit neatly. The TCP/IP model (4 layers) more accurately reflects internet protocol implementation.

questions.question: A CDN caches content at edge locations. At which layer does the caching decision primarily occur?

options.text: Layer 7 - Based on HTTP cache headers

questions.explanation: CDN caching decisions use HTTP headers (Cache-Control, ETag, etc.) which are Layer 7. While routing to edge nodes may use IP geolocation (L3), the caching logic itself is application-layer.

questions.question: Which layer is responsible for end-to-end reliable delivery and flow control?
questions.explanation: Layer 4 (Transport) provides end-to-end communication. TCP specifically handles reliable delivery (acknowledgments, retransmissions) and flow control (windowing). Layer 3 only handles routing.
